meta.tagline: Caribbean-blue sea, granite mountains, and an island that speaks its own language

pills: Sardinia without a car is half an island

overview.title: Welcome to Sardinia
overview.intro: Sardinia is not an island but a small continent: Caribbean-blue coves on the coast, granite mountains inland, three-thousand-year-old stone towers called nuraghi, and a language apart from Italian. The yachts of the Costa Smeralda are the shop window; the real Sardinia lives in shepherd villages, in the crackle of bread, and in the ease of people who say 'ajò' and hit the road. Don't underestimate the distances, don't hurry the sea — this island belongs to slow travellers.

local_word.definition: Sardinian for 'come on, let's go': the island's mood in one word. To the sea, to the mountains, to the table — no matter; say ajò and a Sardinian counts you as one of their own.

rules.title: Rent a car — no negotiation
rules.description: Public transport is weak between the coastal towns; the coves, nuraghi and mountain villages only happen by car. In summer book months ahead; automatics sell out early.

rules.title: Don't tour the island from one base
rules.description: Cagliari to Alghero is four hours. Set separate bases for north, east and south, or devote the trip to one region; the ambition to 'see it all' turns a holiday into motorway.

rules.title: Leave the sand and shells where they are
rules.description: Taking sand, pebbles or shells from the beaches is illegal and seriously fined; suitcases get scanned at the airports. For a souvenir, a photo and a bottle of mirto suffice.

quick_facts.label: Language
quick_facts.sub: In Alghero they even speak Catalan

tip.label: The Sardinia philosophy
tip.text: Sardinians are among the longest-lived peoples on earth and the secret is plain: little hurry, long tables, constant sea air. Count every slow day on the island as a dose of the recipe.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.intro: In Sardinia the plan starts with a car; the rest is choosing coves.

items.title: Arrival — three airports
items.description: Cagliari is the gate to the south, Olbia to the northeast (Costa Smeralda), Alghero to the northwest. Fly to the region your route is built on; transfers across the island take hours.

items.title: Ferry — bring your own car
items.description: Night ferries from Civitavecchia, Livorno and Genoa land at Olbia and Cagliari; bringing your own car can beat summer rental prices. Book the cabin early.

items.title: Rental car — the island's key
items.description: The coast roads are scenic but winding, the inland roads narrow. Fill up between villages, keep coins for beach car parks. A small car wins on the narrow cove lanes.

items.title: The Trenino Verde and the main line
items.description: The main railway runs the Cagliari–Sassari axis, slow but scenic; the historic narrow-gauge 'Trenino Verde' is not transport but an excursion in itself.

items.title: Boats to the coves
items.description: Cala Goloritzé, the La Maddalena archipelago and most hidden coves are best reached from the water: daily boat tours and gommone (dinghy) hire are everywhere. Ask the engine limit for licence-free boats.

callout.label: Beach quota warning
callout.text: Some famous beaches (La Pelosa, Tuerredda, the Goloritzé path) run summer visitor quotas with online booking; check the day before and go early in the morning.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: In Sardinia 'where to stay' really means 'which Sardinia': five regions, five different holidays.

local_word.definition: The stone farmhouse of the Gallura region: most are now agriturismi. Staying in a stazzu means sleeping in shepherd Sardinia, ten minutes from the sea.

items.name: Cagliari — capital of the south
items.description: The Castello citadel quarter, the long Poetto beach and true city life: flights are easy, restaurants full, and the southern coves (Chia, Villasimius) within day-trip range. The most sensible start to an island tour.

items.name: Alghero — the Catalan balcony
items.description: A walled old town with a Catalan past and a coral-craft tradition: sunset on the ramparts at dusk, a boat to Neptune's Grotto at dawn. The sweetest base in the northwest.

items.name: Costa Smeralda / San Teodoro
items.description: The shore of emerald coves and yacht marinas: Porto Cervo is the shop window, San Teodoro and Palau the more grounded alternatives. The La Maddalena boat tours leave from here.

items.name: Ogliastra — Cala Gonone and the east
items.description: The coast of the legendary coves — Goloritzé, Mariolu, Luna: boats, footpaths and the place where the mountain falls into the sea. The region for nature and cove collectors; car and solid shoes required.

items.name: The south coast — Chia/Pula
items.description: Long sands, shallow turquoise water and flamingo lagoons: the south's generous shore for families and calm holidays. Proximity to Cagliari airport is the bonus.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: Sardinia's sea is warm even in September; the real question is the crowd-and-price balance.

items.label: Spring
items.name: The Green Island
items.subtitle: Spring · Flowering maquis, empty coves
items.description: The island greens under the scent of maquis, the trails open, the sea warms in June. Quotas not yet running, prices fair — the best window for trekking and cove-hunting.

callout.label: June tip
callout.text: Mid-June is Sardinia's secret peak: July's sea, May's calm, full sunshine.

items.label: Summer
items.name: Peak Sea
items.subtitle: Summer · Warm coves, full beaches
items.description: The sea is a bath, the evenings are festivals, the famous beaches run quotas. In August half of Italy is on the island: book everything ahead and reach the beaches before 9 am.

callout.label: August warning
callout.text: In Ferragosto week (August 15) the ferries and roads overflow; pin your route to one region that week and avoid long drives.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: Warm Sea, Empty Coves
items.subtitle: Autumn · September is the golden month
items.description: In September the sea holds August's warmth and the beaches stand half empty; October brings the harvest and the village festivals (sagre). The island's smartest season.

callout.label: September tip
callout.text: By mid-September the Goloritzé path quota stops being a worry; the classic morning hike + noon swim happens at full flavour.

items.label: Winter
items.name: The Island's Inner Face
items.subtitle: Winter · Shepherd Sardinia, carnival
items.description: The coastal resorts partly close but the interior lives: the 'Cortes Apertas' events in the Barbagia villages, and in January-February the eerie Mamuthones carnival of Mamoiada. No sea, yet a full island.

callout.label: Carnival tip
callout.text: Seeing the Mamuthones procession in Mamoiada in February is looking into Sardinia's three-thousand-year-old face; you go not as tourist but as witness.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: The Sardinian table is two worlds: the sea's harvest on the coast, the shepherd's kitchen inland — and over both, a crisp leaf of carasau.

local_word.definition: Suckling pig turned for hours over myrtle wood: the feast of the shepherd's kitchen. The real thing is eaten at an agriturismo, ordered ahead — the crackle of its skin is the island's sound.

items.name: Culurgiones
items.description: Handmade dumplings filled with potato, pecorino and mint, sealed like an ear of wheat: the pride of Ogliastra. With butter and sage or tomato sauce — poetry either way.

items.name: Porceddu — agriturismo style
items.description: Suckling pig slowly turned over embers, scented with myrtle: the summit of the shepherd's table. It arrives after an army of antipasti on the agriturismo menu — come hungry.

items.name: Pane carasau and guttiau
items.description: The paper-thin shepherd's bread that keeps for months. Baked with olive oil and salt it becomes guttiau — the first crackle to reach the table.

items.name: Bottarga and the seafood course
items.description: The cured mullet roe of the Cabras lagoon is gold dust over spaghetti; on the coast the sea course stretches through prawns, octopus and fregola.

items.name: Pecorino sardo and honey
items.description: The young sheep's cheese is sweet, the aged one sharp; its pairing with bitter corbezzolo honey is an island classic. The soul of seadas is this same duo.

items.name: Cannonau, Vermentino and mirto
items.description: The strength of Cannonau in the red, the salt of Vermentino in the white; dinner is sealed with the myrtle liqueur mirto. Test the 'wine of long life' legend at the source.
items.tag: The glass sequence · end with mirto

callout.label: The agriturismo rule
callout.text: Once in your life, live a Sardinian agriturismo evening: fixed price, countless plates, house wine by the jug. Eat lightly at noon, and don't surrender before the culurgiones arrive.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Gems
hidden_gems.intro: Behind the postcard coves hides a three-thousand-year-old island; these six fit sea and history into the same day.

items.name: Su Nuraxi — Barumini
items.description: The largest nuraghe complex, UNESCO-listed: a stone tower and village fabric from 1500 BC. Guided tours go inside the tower — the entrance lesson to the island's mysterious civilisation.

items.name: Cala Goloritzé
items.description: Ogliastra's jewel with its granite arch and needle spire: reached only by footpath (quota-controlled) or by swimming in from a boat. The reward is the Mediterranean's purest cove.

items.rarity: A pastel town on a river
items.name: Bosa
items.description: Coloured houses stacked along the Temo river below the Malaspina castle: the island's most photogenic town, left in Alghero's shadow. Also the home of Malvasia wine.

items.name: Orgosolo
items.description: Barbagia's rebel village, an open-air gallery of over 150 political-poetic murals: shepherd Sardinia's voice on the walls. A shepherd's lunch nearby completes the classic.

items.rarity: A palace entered from the sea
items.name: Neptune's Grotto
items.description: The great stalactite cave in Alghero's Capo Caccia cliffs: by the 654-step cliff stairway (Escala del Cabirol) or by boat. Both are part of the show.

items.rarity: An ancient city in the lagoon
items.name: Tharros
items.description: The Phoenician-Roman city set on the sea at the Sinis peninsula: blue behind every column. With the San Giovanni di Sinis church and the mullet shacks nearby, a perfect half day.

callout.label: Combination tip
callout.text: Sardinia's formula is 'stone in the morning, sea at noon': put the nuraghe or ancient city first, then swim in the nearest cove — history and holiday fit the same day.

traps.title: Skip the Traps
traps.intro: Sardinia is an honest island; most traps grow from wrong expectations. Know these four.

items.name: Mistaking the Costa Smeralda for Sardinia
items.description: Porto Cervo's yacht window is one percent of the island; judging the island by those prices — or confining it to them — are both mistakes.
items.instead: Tour the shop window for one coffee, then return to the real island: San Teodoro's coves, Gallura's villages, the inland tables.

items.name: Arriving unplanned at a quota beach
items.description: Reach La Pelosa at noon and you'll watch the sea from behind a rope; in summer the famous coves demand booking.
items.instead: Reserve the quota beaches online a day ahead and arrive at 8; or pick the equally lovely neighbouring cove — this island always has one.

items.name: 'Catalan lobster' with the price unasked
items.description: Alghero's famous lobster sells by the etto (100 g); order without asking and the bill rocks the holiday budget.
items.instead: Agree the weight and etto price up front; or take the same joy at a fair price with fregola and prawns.

items.name: Trusting the map's distances
items.description: An 80 km coast road can take two hours; 'we'll make dinner' plans melt in the bends.
items.instead: Add thirty percent to the app's estimate and do one big drive a day; on Sardinia, fewer roads and more coves is always the right equation.

callout.label: The golden rule
callout.text: The colour of Sardinia's sea is proportional not to your money but to how early you rise: no beach club outshines an empty cove at 8 am.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Routes
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. The times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: The southern classic from a Cagliari base

steps.title: Castello morning
steps.description: Look over the gulf from the ramparts of Cagliari's citadel; coffee around Piazza Yenne, pastry stop permitted.

steps.title: San Benedetto market
steps.description: Descend to the fish floor of one of Italy's biggest covered markets: bottarga, cheese and provisions for lunch.

steps.title: South to the Chia coves
steps.description: Drive the coast road to Chia: turquoise water, white dunes, a flamingo lagoon. Swim at Su Giudeu.

steps.title: Lunch behind the beach
steps.description: Fregola or a panino at a sand-floored chiringuito; then one more cove — Tuerredda if you dare, check its quota.

steps.title: Ancient Nora
steps.description: Stop at the seaside Phoenician-Roman city on the way back: mosaics, theatre and the setting sun in one frame.

steps.title: Cagliari evening
steps.description: A seafood table in the Marina quarter, closed with mirto. Ajò — another cove tomorrow!

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: Live the island as a guest, not a tourist

steps.title: The southern classic
steps.description: The 1-day flow above: Castello, market, Chia, Nora.

steps.title: Stone and the interior
steps.description: Su Nuraxi (Barumini) in the morning, the drive into Barbagia at noon, Orgosolo's murals after; an agriturismo feast at night — porceddu and Cannonau.

steps.title: The eastern coves
steps.description: Rise early for the boat from Cala Gonone along the Goloritzé–Mariolu line: swim, rest, swim again. Sunset aperitivo at Santa Maria Navarrese; farewell with pecorino and honey.

phrases.title: The 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: Italian is enough, but one word of Sardinian opens the doors wide.

items.meaning: Good morning / good day — mandatory entering the village bar
Please — add it to the end of your order
Cheers! — Cannonau glasses rise to this
Sardinian for 'let's go!' — say it once and you count as an islander

items.label: Swim a turquoise cove at 8 am
items.sub: The cove yours, the colours at their purest

items.label: Enter the nuraghe tower at Su Nuraxi
Sit through a porceddu feast at an agriturismo
items.sub: Fixed price, endless plates, house wine

items.label: See the wheat-ear seal on culurgiones
Swim into Goloritzé from a boat
items.sub: Granite arch and needle spire — the purest Mediterranean

items.label: Take the cliff stairway to Neptune's Grotto
items.sub: 654 steps — the price of the view

items.label: Walk Bosa's pastel lanes
items.sub: The Temo riverside + a glass of Malvasia

items.label: Eat spaghetti with bottarga
items.sub: Cabras gold dust — fregola works too

items.label: Close with mirto
items.sub: The myrtle liqueur — and a bottle for the suitcase
